General obligation bonds are issued by states, cities or counties and not secured by any assets. Instead, general obligation are backed by the “full faith and credit” of the issuer, which has the power to tax residents to pay bondholders.
Revenue bonds are not backed by government’s taxing power but by revenues from a specific project or source, such as highway tolls or lease fees.
answer: Municipal bonds differ in where repayment support comes from. A general obligation bond is backed by the issuer’s “full faith and credit” and taxing power, rather than by specific assets. A revenue bond is backed by income from a particular project or source, such as highway tolls or lease fees, not by the government’s taxing power. Some revenue bonds are non-recourse: if their revenue stream dries up, bondholders may have no claim on the underlying revenue source.
